#### Fresh independent part-5 backend review — 2026-10-19

Reviewed issue #445, the approved backend plan, the current handoff, the actual uncommitted backend and consumer diffs, and `CODING_STANDARDS.md`. Code remained read-only. No checks ran.

**Findings for human decision**

- **High — Fountain stack shape is wrong — `data/domain/world-5/hole/fountain.tsx:127–154,324–343`:** v1.23 claim logic iterates `Holes[29][space].length`, values each item at `[space][n]`, and uses the array length for the stack factor (`idleon1.23.txt:269631–269654`). Each saved stack position contains an array of currency IDs, not one ID. `Number([])` becomes zero; `Number([id1,id2])` becomes `NaN`; a one-item array loses its array shape. The importer then counts stack positions by currency instead of counting items in each position. Saved empty and multi-item stacks, occupancy, and pending values are therefore wrong. The focused test checks currency 0, not stack shape or claim values. The approved plan's singular wording at line 20 shares this source-shape error and needs human correction before acceptance.
- **Medium — Cove camp coefficients are unscaled — `data/domain/world-5/hole/hole.tsx:2647–2650`, `data/domain/world-5/hole/cove.ts:283–296`:** `getSchematicBonus` defaults to factor 1. v1.23 respawn uses `B_UPG(100,25)` (`idleon1.23.txt:146232–146237`); pickup doubling uses `B_UPG(101,10)`, `B_UPG(103,10)`, and `B_UPG(105,10)` (`241659–241660`). The current local outputs understate those camp contributions by 25× and 10×. Existing runtime evidence used map 162, not Cove map 216; focused tests do not verify these outputs.
- **Medium — Fountain keeps raw setting and slot state — `fountain.tsx:113–119,155–170`:** `ignoredCurrenciesEncoded` exposes the raw save encoding instead of named ignored-currency IDs. `holes11Index7` also carries a save-position name into the currency calculation. `PARSE-01` requires translating save representation at the boundary. Existing evidence describes ignored currencies as generation exclusions, but does not establish the encoding grammar or a player/domain name for slot 7; do not invent either.
- **Low — impossible missing-object branches — `fountain.tsx:351–354,396–404`:** `getLuckyCoinChance` optional-chains the fixed currency catalogue. `canAffordOpal` checks `undefined` after `available` guarantees a valid index in the nine-wallet array, and its `getOpalCost() === null` fallback repeats the only condition that can make the cost null. `DATA-01` and `SIMPLE-01` call for direct access to initialized records and guards only for genuinely missing save values.

#### Fountain display questions — 2026-10-20

- **Resource value / overflow / Lucky chance:** UI prints `getCurrencyValue(currency.index)`, `getOverflowValue(currency.index)`, and `getLuckyCoinChance(currency.index) × 100` (`components/world-5/hole/part4Caverns.tsx:252–264`). Value is one currency item's current Fountain valuation, not wallet balance: domain combines base and water-wallet multiplier with all-currency, desire, Lucky-coin-count, and duck multipliers; currency IDs 6+ use square root of desire × base × all multiplier (`fountain.tsx:443–474`). Overflow getter is exactly per-item currency value × Keep multiplier (`488–491`); this establishes displayed calculation only, not when it is awarded, whether it is retained upon clearing/full stacks, or what event triggers Keep. Those game-event semantics remain unresolved.
- **Desire selection:** saved `[11][82]` becomes `desireCurrencyId` (`fountain.tsx:291–292`); it is the selected currency identity. The desire multiplier boosts that chosen currency, and IDs 6+ (`466–472`). It changes value, not currency identity/count. UI displays selected name separately (`part4Caverns.tsx:267–269`); no claim of highlight behavior is supported by this view.
- **Value exponent:** saved `[11][7]` is parsed as `currencyValueExponent` (`fountain.tsx:261,304`). v1.23 source `idleon1.23.txt:241504–517` applies `1.1^value` to valuation. It changes resulting currency value, not currency IDs or item count. Underlying benefit is multiplicative value scaling; no player-facing game name is established. Raw exponent is an explanatory factor, not a resource balance.
- Pending value: preparation computes each item's stack value from its currency value, stack length, and Royal status (`fountain.tsx:313–327,493–506`); pending aggregate sums each saved stack's value (`508–516`). This domain sum alone does not establish a common unit or the actual game's reward destination. Retract the earlier claim that mixed currencies convert to a common Fountain-value scalar. Actual collected-stack reward consumer and wallet destination remain unverified here. This is a saved snapshot; selecting desire influences current calculated per-item values, but the pending snapshot is calculated during preparation, not a promise of future reward or conversion on claim (`part4Caverns.tsx:321`).
- **Positions and capacity:** occupied is count of saved positions with nonempty item arrays (`fountain.tsx:480–482`); capacity is `min(16,1+bonus(0,10))` (`406–409`); open is `max(0,capacity−occupied)` (`484–486`). Effective capacity UI repeats capacity and maximum stack size, not a separate state: `min(50,3+bonus(0,11)+B upgrade 97 level 3+Cosmo bonus quantity 4)` (`411–415`). Thus occupied/capacity plus open are related and algebraically redundant when under capacity, while effective capacity adds per-position item limit. Saved positions can exceed effective capacity; unused trailing saved slots do not increase it.
- **Retained fixture relevance / evidence limit:** Existing paired v1.23 extraction remains latest account evidence: 30 saved positions, 15 occupied, 615 items, capacity 15, hence 0 open; it does not attest current-upgrade Lucky chance. UI lines were inspected directly. Runtime `/status` and `/game-version` confirmed ready offline v1.23. Native query failed HTTP 500; no live access, save mutation, code edit, or test/check run. Fixture remains relevant to space arithmetic, not current lucky-zero diagnosis.

#### Fountain Lucky chance — latest fixture correction — 2026-10-20

- The latest fixture has positive Lucky chance for all nine currencies; the UI's `notateNumber` formatter displays `0%` for each because it floors values below 100 to an integer (`part4Caverns.tsx:22–24,263`; `utility.tsx:457–462`). This corrects the earlier unverified zero-chance hypothesis.
- `Fountain.parse` maps `Holes[31]` to upgrade levels, `Holes[32]` to marbleization levels, and `Holes[30][currencyId]` to each currency's Lucky-coin count (`hole.tsx:2025–2027`; `fountain.tsx:281–284,305–310`). Upgrade repository identifies `(2,8)` as Luck fo' REAL and `(2,10)` as Lucky Ducky; each has bonus-per-level 1 (`FountainUpgradeRepo.ts:633–645,659–670`). Bonus is rounded `marbleBonus × level × bonusPerLevel`; marbleization level 0 gives factor 1 (`fountain.tsx:77–79,214–217`).
- Fixture raw inputs: `latest.json` selector `.Holes|fromjson|.[31][2][8]` = 29, `.[32][2][8]` = 0; `(2,10)` = level 15, marbleization 0. Thus Luck fo' REAL bonus=29 and Lucky Ducky bonus=15. Lucky counts are `.Holes|fromjson|.[30][0:9]` = `[0,1,-1,-1,-1,-1,-1,-1,-1]`. The parser uses these values directly, including saved `-1`.
- `getLuckyCoinChance` returns exact zero only when Luck fo' REAL bonus is zero; otherwise chance=`0.001 × (1+(bonus(2,8)+bonus(2,10))/100) × 0.25^count` (`fountain.tsx:523–530`). Typed `getBonus` rounds marbleization factor × level × bonus-per-level; with marbleization 0 and bonus-per-level 1, fixture levels 29 and 15 give bonuses 29 and 15 (`fountain.tsx:77–79,214–217`; `FountainUpgradeRepo.ts:633–645,659–670`). Thus expression is `0.00144 × 0.25^count`: counts `[0,1,-1,-1,-1,-1,-1,-1,-1]` produce Bronze 0.00144 (0.144%), Silver 0.00036 (0.036%), and each remaining currency 0.00576 (0.576%). UI multiplies by 100, then default formatter floors each percentage below 100, so all display `0%`.
- Fixture-specific, not proven to be the current live profile. Latest fixture selectors are supported; runtime identity evidence does not prove server loaded this fixture (`runtime-access.1.23.json:5–8`). Domain expression and exact fixture arithmetic are established; no verified v1.23 game-source capture for this exact calculation was captured, so game-source equivalence remains unestablished.

#### Fountain unlock ordering — 2026-10-20

- `FountainUpgradeRepo` has 60 records, 20 per water, indexed by `(waterIndex,index)`. Its array order groups by water and then index; it is not unlock order.
- Actual website-domain unlock condition: `FountainUpgrade.isUnlocked` treats negative `prerequisiteIndex` as unlocked. Otherwise it finds an upgrade with equal `waterIndex` and `index === prerequisiteIndex`; required level is 10 except Yellow Water indices 2 and 14, which require level 1 (`data/domain/world-5/hole/fountain.tsx:223–232`). This proves `prerequisiteIndex` names upgrade identity within that water, not UI position. `uiPosition` is separate coordinate text; code does not use it in unlock checks.
- Static fields for all records expose no separately named prerequisite-level field. The operative level thresholds above come from code, not static `requiredLevel`. Roots are Yellow index 9 Fountain Filling (`prerequisiteIndex=-1`), Green index 10 Marble Filling (`-1`), and Red index 12 Rubber Ducky (`-1`). Other sentinels are absent. Repository has no `requiredLevel` field in `FountainUpgradeModel` (`data/domain/model/fountainUpgradeModel.ts:3–11`).
- All edges below point prerequisite → dependent. Each water has branching rooted DAG, not single chain. Vertices are `(waterIndex:index)`; each dependent uses source threshold 10, except Yellow dependents 2 and 14 use 1:
  - Yellow (water 0): root `9`; edges `9→2,14; 2→10,12; 12→3; 3→5,11; 5→8; 8→4; 4→1,19; 19→6; 6→0,7; 14→16; 16→15; 15→17; 17→18; 18→13`.
- Green (water 1): root `10`; prerequisite → dependent edges `10→2,14; 2→12; 12→3; 3→5; 5→8; 8→9; 9→4,11; 4→1,6; 1→0; 0→7; 6→19; 14→16; 16→15; 15→17; 17→18; 18→13`.
- Red (water 2): root `12`; prerequisite → dependent edges `12→2,14; 2→8; 8→3,11; 3→5; 5→1; 1→4,19; 4→6; 6→0; 19→7; 11→9,10; 14→16; 16→17; 17→15; 15→18; 18→13`.

Treat water availability as its own gate, not as interleaved upgrade edges. #### Cove local-output gating research — 2026-10-19

**Website answer:** Cove outputs are prepared for every imported player; they are not hidden or returned `null` merely because that player is outside the Cove. `Hole.updateHoleCharacterCapabilities` calls `hole.cove.prepareCharacters` for all players (`data/domain/world-5/hole/hole.tsx:2634–2653`), passing each player's saved `currentMapId`, persistent cavern assignment (`characterAssignments[playerID]`, or `-1`), and camp bonuses. `Cove.prepare` defines Cove context as map 216 and cavern 17 (`data/domain/world-5/hole/cove.ts:251–253`).

| Output | Website behavior outside map 216 + cavern 17 | Actual calculation / use |
|---|---|---|
| Drop rate | Returns neutral multiplier `1`, not zero/null; in Cove calculates a multiplier, or `null` if required imported Cove inputs are unavailable (`cove.ts:255–301`). | Prospective local capability is prepared regardless of current map. |
| AFK gain | Returns `0`; in Cove calculates `(10 + upgrades 8 + 13)/100`, or `null` for unavailable levels (`cove.ts:270–303`). | Prospective local capability is prepared regardless of current map. |
| Multikill per damage tier and base multikill | Each returns `0`; in Cove calculates upgrade 6 / 15 bonus divided by 100, or `null` if unavailable (`cove.ts:272–307`). | Prospective local capability is prepared regardless of current map. |
| Respawn | Returns neutral multiplier `1`; in Cove calculates reciprocal of `1 + (upgrade 2 + camp upgrade 100)/100`, or `null` if inputs unavailable (`cove.ts:274,308–310`). | Prospective local capability is prepared regardless of current map. |
| Pickup | Outside Cove returns no target, known target state, and amount `0`; random-double chance is `0`. In Cove, selected targets and amounts depend on target availability, unlock bonus, balance, and camp bonuses (`cove.ts:276–325`). | Prospective local capability is prepared regardless of current map. |

These neutral/zero outside-context values are a concrete WEBSITE calculation defect for prospective Cove-local display: `prepare` gates the calculated values using each character's current map and saved assignment. The current UI can only show `localEffectsByPlayerId`'s gated values; it cannot show prospective values for characters saved elsewhere. This is distinct from unavailable saved inputs, which correctly produce `null` for dependent calculations. The returned object mixes “calculated capability” with “applies here” state; its `appliesInCove` flag does not preserve the would-be Cove calculation outside the gate.

**Game evidence and limits:** v1.23 source explicitly applies Cove respawn on the `caveD` branch, calculating `MonsterDefinitionsGET.caveD.RespawnTime / (1 + (Cglunko_Respawn(0,0) + B_UPG(100,25))/100)` and assigning the result to `caveC.RespawnTime` (`idleon1.23.txt:146232–237`). This is application-time behavior, distinct from whether helper operands can be calculated elsewhere. The branch predicate shown is `g == "caveD"`; this excerpt does not establish map ID 216, cavern ID 17, or persistent character-assignment checks. Source does not prove helper callability outside Cove, nor source predicates for drop, AFK, multikill, or pickup consumers. Do not infer those restrictions from map ID alone.

No fresh runtime comparison was made. The retained v1.23 offline runtime was character 3 (`Sludgev4`) in scene 162, not Cove. Earlier attempt to call `Holes2.Cove_CrystalGlunkoDropRate(0,0)` returned invalid `69`; scene/player accessors failed. That value is not a Cove observation and must not be used as a comparison. Genuine comparison values require valid player/scene selection in Cove map 216 and cavern 17, with imported save operands matched to the game queries. No scene transition, save mutation, or purchase occurred. Other game consumer restrictions and helper call shape remain unverified.

#### Harp Opal chance input limit — v1.23 source

- The source formula uses `Holes[7][5]` Harp Opals and saved power through `GenINFO[112]`, plus Stringy Effect's +15 percentage points, Domino Effect's +20 points per string activation (`GenINFO[128]`), and Variety Effect's +30 points per distinct string (`GenINFO[129]`) (`idleon1.23.txt:241038–45,241065–75,261983–96`; upgrade records `HoleBuildingRepo.ts:379–407`).
- `GenINFO[128]` counts newly activated strings and resets at a power-cycle boundary (`idleon1.23.txt:268037–108`). The parser does not import cycle phase history (`hole.tsx:1566–1597`), and the prepared API exposes no current activation count (`1600–1617`). The account snapshot therefore cannot yield exact current chance when Domino Effect is owned without an unsupported cycle assumption. `GenINFO[129]` counts distinct raw saved assignment values and is derivable from a complete saved layout (`idleon1.23.txt:268332–40`); it is not the missing activation counter.
- Source review is bounded and does not establish runtime parity or prove absence of all alias/save-restore paths. No exact instantaneous chance calculation was added; the subsequently approved zero-plucked baseline is implemented as recorded below.

#### Harp Opal competitor research correction — 2026-10-18

- Research in [Toolbox's Harp parser](../../reference-repos/IdleonToolbox/parsers/world-5/caverns/the-harp.ts) found Toolbox computes one saved-state chance using first 11 active layout slots, distinct values including zero, Opals `[7][5]`, saved power `[11][22]`, owned schematic factors, and zero Domino activation count by default (`reference-repos/IdleonToolbox/parsers/world-5/caverns/the-harp.ts:14–24,142–161`; parser mapping `parsers/world-5/hole.ts:72–109`).
- **Correction:** Exact arbitrary-instant strum chance remains unknown without transient progress. But a deterministic saved-state baseline is calculable using zero activated strings, matching Toolbox's explicit default—not by assuming completed strum. The configured save yields `0.8541193272644844%` under that convention. This is isolated-expression evidence, not competitor module/runtime/game parity.

### Part 4 phase 5 independent backend review — 2026-10-17

Read-only review of issue #444, approved backend plan, scoped current diff, coding standards, focused tests, and assigned v1.23 source. No checks were rerun.

**Findings for human decision**

- **Normal-import missing-state collapse — `hole.tsx:2187–2189,2315,2359`:** `holeData` replaces absent rows with empty arrays before calling Lamp and Harp parsers. Missing Wish 1 reset-target rows therefore look like known-empty arrays; missing Harp assignments set `layoutAvailable` to `true`. Existing missing-data tests call aspect parsers directly and miss this normal-import boundary. Preserve absent rows for these aspects and assert this through a normal import. This violates the plan's unknown-versus-zero requirement and `PARSE-01`.
- **Harp note access excludes the highest unlocked note — `hole.tsx:1529`:** v1.23 `Holes[11][20]` is the highest selectable note index, not a count. ### Part 4 phase 5 independent backend review — 2026-10-17

Read-only review of issue [#444](https://github.com/Sludging/idleon-efficiency/issues/444), the approved [backend plan](hole-part-4-backend-plan.md), current handoff, coding standards, scoped backend changes, existing pipeline interfaces, and focused tests. **Findings for human decision**

- **Unknown versus zero — `well.tsx:69–74`:** Missing sediment stock sets `unavailable` to `false`. A missing value is unknown, not known spendable stock; the separate `current` field is null, but this boolean can still report the opposite of the required unavailable/unknown state.
- **Unknown versus zero — `hole.tsx:1564–1573`:** Missing saved wish levels become zero, and Wish 5 discount is then calculated as 1. The Wish repository guarantees twelve static wish records, not that every imported save contains twelve saved levels. This also makes missing level data look like unpurchased wishes and produces costs from a false zero. The focused test repeats the zero fallback at `part4-pipeline.test.ts:100–102`.
- **Partial Harp outcome — `hole.tsx:1541–1543`:** Harp exposes power/hour, assignments, and permanent string bonuses, but no current assigned-string trigger effects or their random/order-sensitive context. The approved plan requires Harp active/passive effects (`hole-part-4-backend-plan.md:57`) and says to include relevant reward context without promising a fixed result. The source formulas are not a license to simulate rewards; the plan should clarify whether current-state effect/chance outputs are required.
- **Duplicated slot calculation — `hole.tsx:1526–1533` and `1822–1829`:** `Harp.prepare` recomputes slot count and dependencies already calculated by `prepareSharedUpgradeEffects` and fed to schematics. This creates two owners for the same result and risks disagreement; the approved integration names the existing `holeUpgradeEffects` stage as slot preparation.
- **Backend presentation geometry — `hole.tsx:1474,1535–1539`:** `Harp.slotPositions` adds pixel coordinates and breakpoints to the backend. The game source confirms these are renderer positions (`idleon1.23.txt:241025–30`); the approved outcome requires saved layout/slots, not screen coordinates. This is frontend overfitting and premature presentation work.
- **Impossible static-record guard — `hole.tsx:1573,1598`:** `this.wishes[5]` is guarded despite `LampWishRepo` supplying all twelve records and the aspect building wishes from that repository. This conflicts with `DATA-01`; use direct access for required initialized records.
- **Unused Harp input — `hole.tsx:1478,1488,1524–1525`:** Harp stores Gaming's Cglunko bonus but does not consume it in any approved current-state result. Source uses Cglunko in reward production, which this work excludes. Keep the owner getter for Well; remove Harp-only state unless a required result consumes it.

These tests do not assert calculation outputs against independent game values. The plan requires zero-tolerance, same-save v1.23 parity for these calculations. Do not infer saved mode access from a fixed four-mode UI list.
- **Harp passives:** Game UI explicitly says level bonuses “are permanent and work at all times,” while assigned slots separately determine which strings claim on a Harp trigger (261980–96, 264267–301, 265615–20). - **H40 — P2: Missing Measurement inputs lose availability in Gambit.** `data/domain/world-5/hole/hole.tsx:1966` supplies unavailable Death Note points when optional character `KLA_` input is missing. `Measurement.prepare` records unavailable statistics but stores a zero fallback at line 922. The plan, line 61, requires: **“Preserve secondary-link rules and callers that count only primary links.”** **Recommendation for decision:** Obtain eligible ordinary activation from its Divinity owner. ### Part 2 phase 5 independent backend review

**Authority and method (2026-10-15):** Fresh, read-only review covers selected part 2 [#442](https://github.com/Sludging/idleon-efficiency/issues/442), its published approval, the [backend plan](hole-part-2-backend-plan.md), and the [approved specification](hole-spec-draft.md). Followed phase 5 of the [feature workflow](../human/feature-workflow.md), `code-review`, architecture guidance, [CODING_STANDARDS.md](../../CODING_STANDARDS.md), [CONTRIBUTING.md](../../CONTRIBUTING.md), domain discovery, and existing Hole vocabulary. Isolated axes ran serially: `HolePart2BackendReview.HoleP2Standards`, then `HolePart2BackendReview.HoleP2Spec`. Plan approval was not treated as a standards exception.

**Comparison scope:** Baseline `HEAD` is `31f1513731defa60a854125390f268924bcd9db9`. Selected backend changes are uncommitted. Reviewed `git diff HEAD --` for Hole, Villager, pipeline registration, Divinity, Companions, Tome, Farming, and the affected part 1 pipeline test. Also reviewed the eight new selected-part suites, helper, extraction configs/results, and relevant producer/consumer contracts. Supplied generated building/currency exports were read-only prerequisite context, not attributed to the implementation worker. Unrelated Research, Spelunking, navigation, generated exports, and unrelated test edits were excluded.

#### Standards

- **H36 — P2, MODEL-01: Majiks owns individual upgrade progression behavior.** `data/domain/world-5/hole/hole.tsx:314–326` computes and writes each `CosmoUpgrade`'s initial/enhancement levels, access, cap, predecessor state, and purchase eligibility inside `Majiks.prepare`. The upgrade stores these fields but cannot prepare its own progression. A rule change spans both the container and responsible concept. [MODEL-01](../../CODING_STANDARDS.md#model-01--model-responsible-concepts) requires aspect update logic and game calculations on the aspect class; the plan's responsibilities at lines 21–22 do not waive that rule. **Recommendation for decision:** Let `CosmoUpgrade` prepare its progression from the pool, access, gate, and predecessor inputs supplied by `Majiks`.
- **H37 — P2, PARSE-01: Raw Majik tree encoding survives parsing.** `hole.tsx:293–297` retains the original save arrays in `investments`. Calculation later converts their values with `Number` at line 308 and reads predecessors through `[tree][treePosition - 1]` at line 322. The calculation still depends on raw save layout, despite parsed upgrade records. This violates [PARSE-01](../../CODING_STANDARDS.md#parse-01--translate-at-the-boundary) and the plan's line 35 boundary. **Recommendation for decision:** Translate predecessor state and complete numeric investment inputs during parsing, including undisplayed placeholder investments. Calculate from named state rather than retained save arrays.
- **H38 — P3, non-blocking smell judgement: Pocket inspection repeats the Doot eligibility rule.** `hole.tsx:235–241` recomputes companion ownership plus the character's Divinity-level gate. `data/domain/companions.tsx:121–125` already prepares that rule as `PlayerDivinityInfo.dootActive`, which `data/domain/world-5/divinity.tsx:222–226` consumes. Late Pocket inspection runs after both updates. This is **Duplicated Code / possible Feature Envy**, not a separate hard violation. Two production owners must now maintain the same gate. **Recommendation for decision:** Consume prepared eligibility for existing Divinity records; retain genuine missing-save handling.

**Standards verdict:** Two documented P2 breaches remain, plus one P3 maintainability judgement. No further substantiated scope expansion, speculative framework, frontend-shaped state, manufactured description, or impossible initialized-object absence guard was found.

#### Specification

- **H39 — P2: Missing schematic input becomes a false zero Contented Creator benefit.** `hole.tsx:1467` counts built flags and supplies a plain numeric total to `Majiks.prepare`. If optional `Holes[13]` is absent while Village Majik investment exists, `Schematic.parse` sets all flags false (`352–354`). `CosmoUpgrade.getEffects` then exposes a known `0%` benefit (`163–164`), and `getDescription` substitutes that false total (`187`). Saved Majik progression remains known; its schematic-dependent benefit does not. Existing villager growth already marks this dependency unavailable (`1620,1644,1671`). The backend plan, line 65, requires: **“A genuinely missing optional save input makes only dependent values unavailable. Retain independent progression and known zeroes.”** The product specification, line 48, likewise says **“Unknown inputs must not become zero.”** **Recommendation for decision:** Preserve construction-count availability and leave the dependent effect/placeholder unavailable without hiding saved Majik progression. Current complete-save tests do not exercise this path.

**Specification verdict:** One P2 defect remains. Apart from H39, inspected implementation and assertions support released schematic order/availability, full currency joins, current price formulas, the shared Majik pool and caps, Pocket deduplication, and all 17 Measurement mappings, units, and formulas. Early shared preparation precedes affected consumers; late inspection does not feed shared calculations. Tome and Farming producer changes serve required numeric statistics, not another feature. Descriptions derive from generated static text and verified placeholder materialization. No new UI, allocation model, forecast, character-stat engine, or unrelated feature was introduced.

Earlier owner-link, URL-selection, contributor-table, and automatic scroll/focus requirements are superseded. Followed the scoped UI guide, `code-review`, Impeccable context, `CODING_STANDARDS.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, and domain vocabulary discovery. Standards and specification assessments used separate agents in serial order. Approval was not treated as a standards exception.

Reviewed current uncommitted production content with `git diff f9efbcf5 -- app/world-5/hole/content.tsx`. The reviewed content SHA-256 is `e0193d66c398b7caf71e9ad72e1bad1f07f66792cd881424ee1d2e8e61f88902`, matching the retained production evidence source. The route wrapper and both accepted Hole backend sources have no diff from `41f29730`. Unrelated Research and Spelunking work is excluded.

#### Standards

- **H31 — P3, CONSIST-01: Labeled row fields bypass DataRow's label ownership.** `content.tsx:220–223,275–276` uses `kind: "content", label: null` for Level, Invested Opals, stored progress, and rate fields, then renders labels inside `TextAndLabel`. The row guide reserves `label: null` for genuinely unlabeled content (`ui-rows.md:16–17`) and assigns compact label/value typography to DataRow (`24–26`). The UI guide also distinguishes wrappers outside DataRow from its private row rendering (`ui-patterns.md:101–104`). The result is readable and matches the approved preview, but shared row-label changes will not reach these fields. Use text fields for simple values and labeled content fields for genuinely rich values. Keep the selected progression grouping and tooltip behavior. The plan's stronger value hierarchy does not exempt field composition from the shared contract.
- **H32 — P3, DATA-01 / SIMPLE-01: UI revalidates guaranteed Statue contributor metadata.** `content.tsx:52–56` checks contributor count, owner encoding, value identity, unit, and combination. `Villager.prepareCharacterRates` always appends exactly one Statue contributor with those fixed fields (`villager.tsx:341–369`), including when saved Statue input is missing. This duplicates the producer contract in the view and makes a metadata change require another maintenance step. Remove guaranteed-structure validation, not genuine missing-value/reason checks or the complete numeric comparison required by the plan. The typed-input `typeof` checks and the post-completeness null-input recheck are redundant defenses in the same concern. Finite-value checks, nullable saved inputs, and the local account-loading guard remain justified.

#### Specification

- **H33 — P2: Useful nonzero growth modifiers are no longer inspectable.** The whitelist at `content.tsx:201–209` retains only purchased EXP, role multiplier, Equal Spread, Opal Enthusiasm, and the bundle, besides the separately shown Statue. All other shared growth sources disappear, with no surviving shared context. The approved plan says **“Keep useful nonzero modifiers”** (`ui-plan.md:17`) and retains **“useful advanced context”** in decision 5 (`70`). Real-save records include Bravery **8,314.38%**, Grimoire **172.5%**, Arcade **9.23%**, and other material contributors. The full-size `rate-0-rounded.png` shows that none appear. Players can read the rate but cannot inspect those sources. Preserve useful nonzero shared modifiers once in concise tooltip context. Do not restore repeated contributor tables, owner metadata, zeros, or neutral multipliers. The approved preview contains the same omission; visual agreement alone does not satisfy the written outcome.

| 5. Advanced rate tooltips | Partial: H33. Growth details buttons are removed and conventional tooltips work, but useful shared modifiers are discarded. |
| 6. Deduplication | Met for repeated descriptions/effect tables, zero source/location rows, neutral modifiers, repeated status, and contributor inventories. H33 identifies over-pruning, not a request to restore those inventories. |
| 7. Value hierarchy | Visually met. Aligned progression groups and stronger values match the approved render. H31 remains a separate shared-row standards issue. |

Complete unrounded records agree across all 55 villager/character contexts, yielding immediate rates for all 11 imported characters. Differing/unavailable fixtures retain truthful ranges, optional named inspection, matched Statue context, and visible missing-input reasons. No account-wide rate claim appears. |

#### Standards

- **H27 — P3, LANG-01: Player-facing details expose implementation terms instead of their meaning.** `app/world-5/hole/content.tsx:269-271` first translates the effect type, then prints raw `owned-study-contribution` and `owned-study-rule` scope tokens. It also renders domain notes verbatim. Actual Fountain detail `12-study-16-detail-expanded.png` says “The delivered marbleization caller checks upgrade exclusions without a Study check.” Wisdom detail `12-study-13-detail-expanded.png` refers to “The round caller.” Cove detail and its owner viewport repeat raw scope tokens. Other authored labels expose “typed effects,” “The backend floors,” and raw owner tokens (`content.tsx:286,338,370,396,430`). These require knowledge of implementation internals, contrary to LANG-01. Show readable scope and source names. Explain the established player-facing restrictions without caller/backend terminology. Preserve the divisor rule, Wisdom capacity condition, and Fountain owned-effect versus full eligibility distinction; do not replace them with a stronger game-benefit claim or change accepted calculations.
- **H28 — P3, DATA-01: The saved-time object has an impossible absence branch.** `content.tsx:171` casts `timeAway` as `| undefined` and uses `?.GlobalTime` after the loaded-data gate. `data/domain/idleonData.tsx:419` creates that map entry unconditionally; line `423` directly accesses the parsed object's `GlobalTime` before the import completes. `lib/stores/appDataStore.tsx:191-192,207-208` publishes `StaticData`/`LiveData` only after that import. The outer object is therefore required on this path. Remove only its artificial optionality. Retain checks for a genuinely missing or invalid saved timestamp field. This is a maintainability finding, not a demonstrated wrong timestamp.
- **H29 — P3, READ-01: The Study effect field combines too many view responsibilities in one expression.** `content.tsx:393` combines the effect loop, two semantic-caveat branches, detail selection/navigation, and the owner link inside one field expression. Lines `276-277` similarly mix pinned-owner inclusion, access filtering, description materialization, effect-label search, and normalization. Correct behavior still leaves these independently meaningful rules difficult to inspect or change. Use explicit named view steps or a small local summary renderer. No new generic framework, options layer, or broad component migration is needed. This finding concerns responsibility clarity, not line length or formatter-enforced style.

#### Specification

- **H30 — P2: Exact owner links open content without bringing the owner into view.** The plan's lines `60,66` require a cavern link back to its exact Study detail. `content.tsx:175-187` routes every internal owner link with `scroll: false`, without a fragment or a destination-scroll/focus step. Studies still render all preceding rows (`386-420`). The production `09-studies-actual-first-viewport.png` shows only Studies 1–3; Cove's Study 18 return link appears near the bottom of `13-cove-owner-actual-viewport.png`. Selecting it opens Study 18 below 17 preceding rows instead of presenting the selected detail. The full-ledger owner has the same issue below five villager rows. This is source-confirmed missing destination presentation; the exact post-click viewport consequence is inferred from the code and retained composition, not freshly reproduced. The retained scenario checks `target.waitFor({ state: 'visible' })` at `scenario.cjs:136-145,353-361,492-494`; Playwright visibility permits offscreen elements. Those passing assertions establish rendered/query selection, not owner discoverability. Bring the selected owner into view after rendering, including direct query links and reload, without changing the catalogue or adding a new navigation model.

### Phase 5 independent backend review

**Authority and scope (2026-10-13):** Reviewed selected part 1, [#441](https://github.com/Sludging/idleon-efficiency/issues/441), against the amended backend plan. #### Standards

- **H1 — P2, MODEL-01: Villager does not own its complete growth preparation.** `data/domain/world-5/hole/hole.tsx:1199-1276` computes role-specific growth rules, availability, and contributor records. `villager.tsx:185-198` receives those results and performs the final multiplication. Polonai and Cosmo role rules therefore remain in the parent. This splits one aspect's behavior across two owners, despite the plan's Villager responsibility. Keep shared inputs and allocation in Hole. Put role-specific preparation and contributor construction on Villager; no new role framework is needed.
- **H2 — P3, DATA-01: Required Pristine Charm has an impossible absence fallback.** `hole.tsx:1590,1621` uses `pristineCharm?.unlocked` to substitute zero when the record is absent. Sneaking creates every delivered Pristine Charm during parsing (`world-6/sneaking.tsx:457-466`). Candy Cache, item ID 21, is a required catalogue record (`data/NinjaItemRepo.ts:837-845`). Treat that record as required. Keep the real unowned-charm branch, not a catalogue-absence branch.
- **H3 — P3, UPDATE-01: Early shared preparation includes display-only calculations.** `hole.tsx:1051-1068` prepares next intrinsic unlocks and the Another Try inspection summary in `postProcessingMap` (`idleonData.tsx:273`). These outputs have no calculation consumers. The standard places UI-only calculations in `postPostProcessingMap`. Keep early Study/schematic inputs and Tome's cavern total early. Prepare unlock/reset inspection data in the existing late Hole step.

These are documented-standard findings, not heuristic smell claims. No generic modifier framework, new account-data model, excessive test seam, or independently actionable abstraction smell was confirmed.

#### Specification

- **H4 — P2: Unknown Superbit ownership becomes inactive neighbor rates.** `hole.tsx:1617` passes a Boolean ownership value without saved-input availability. `gaming/palette.ts:41-49` defaults absent `Gaming[12]` to unpurchased. With a known target and accessible neighbors, Hole then publishes no eligible neighbors and zero neighbor accrual. This violates outcome 3 and the plan's missing-input rule. Preserve the known target rate. Mark only potentially eligible neighbor participation/rates unavailable when ownership input is genuinely missing.
- **H5 — P2: Missing Majik state becomes zero allocation effects.** `hole.tsx:1173-1184` checks villager inputs but not the required Village Majik state. Parsing absent `Holes[5]` assigns Majik levels zero (`1402-1404`). Equal Spread and Opal Enthusiasm then report zero with no missing-input reason, although growth rates correctly become unavailable. This violates outcome 2. Preserve known least investment and invested tens. Make the dependent percentages unavailable when their Majik input is missing.
- **H6 — P2: Missing card save still produces complete growth rates.** The growth availability list (`hole.tsx:1376-1387`) omits `Cards0`, while growth consumes Gloomie card level (`1196,1625`). Cards defaults an absent save to `{}` and missing counts to zero (`cards.tsx:228-247`). A genuinely absent card save can therefore publish numeric rates and a zero card contributor with no reason. This violates outcome 1. Track card-save availability and mark dependent rates/contributions unavailable; retain a real zero from a present save.
- **H7 — P2: Cross-skilling effect names describe the wrong numeric meaning.** `Study.getEffects()` (`hole.tsx:379-385`) labels `bonus * completedLayers` as a percentage requirement reduction. Captured values are 570%, 1870%, 3420%, and 972%. Original `Holes/TotalOreREQ` divides requirements by `1 + (collectible bonus + summed Study contributions) / 100`. These values are additive denominator bonuses, not literal percentage reductions. The config's `study_effects_1/7/11/16` expressions reproduce that intermediate arithmetic, so passing tests do not validate the label. Name the owned divisor contribution accurately and explain its additive combination. Do not claim a complete cavern requirement or invent a new calculator.

H4–H6 are source-proven missing-input branches, not exercised runtime failures. H7 concerns the observed API values and their source-backed meaning. The approved plan does not exempt these contracts from standards or permit unknown inputs to become zero.

## 1. What The Hole does

The Hole is entered from the right side of World 5's Mister Brightside map. Its campfire opens villager features. Polonai opens deeper caverns; other villagers are rescued within them. The loop is: collect resources and Opals, allocate Opals to villager growth, gain levels and unlocks, spend competing resources on improvements, then gain better production and rewards. Active challenges, passive production, character skilling, and account upgrades are different parts of that loop. [P1, W1, G1, G3]

Current scope is **18 released caverns across four biome groups**. `CavernsOwned` returns `min(18, PolonaiLevel)`. Publisher releases corroborate Fountain/Trench as 16/17 and Crystal Glunko Cove as 18. Extra source slots, a fourth monument, Elder/unknown villagers, and future reward descriptions do not establish released content. Historical launch had ten caverns/four villagers. Historical Wisdom news calls it cavern 12; current ordering is **Evertree 12, Wisdom 13**. [G1, G18, W1, W4, P1–P3]

### Ownership and meaning

Most progression lives in account-wide `Holes`, alongside separate `Jars` and account options. However, `Holes[0][characterIndex]` records each character's cavern assignment. Character skill efficiency, combat, inventory, and AFK inputs remain character-specific. A shared cavern progress total does not identify each character's contribution or current activity. [G3, G5, G6, G13, G16, O1]

| Distinction | Meaning for website information |
|---|---|
| Saved progression versus possible reward | A built flag, purchased level, earned Opal, or claimed milestone is owned progression. A static description or unlocked reward is not proof it was earned. [G3, G7, G15] |
| Stored progress versus claimed level | Villager EXP and Study progress can exceed their next requirement before camp UI converts them into levels. Show saved level and claim-ready progress separately. [G3, G5] |
| Stock versus work | Sediment, notes, Rupies, wishes, torches, shapes, and Fountain wallet balances are spendable stocks. Skilling materials gathered toward a layer are dedicated cavern progress, not ordinary inventory stacks. [G6, G9, G10, G13, G16, G17] |
| Saved settings versus actor selection | Harp layout/tune, Bell mode, Study target, and boosted Cove shapes have saved settings. Selected UI tabs, highlighted upgrades, reset target, and active minigame choices are actor-only state. [G3, G9, G10, G12, G16] |
| Imported state versus live state | A save supports an as-recorded view. It does not establish live Fear, court coins, a memory board, pending story rewards, or elapsed production since import. [G6, G7, G12, G14, O1] |

Hypothetical allocations, manual court flags, simulated layouts, or website-selected actors are user inputs, not discovered save fields. Browsing a character row must not imply the website changed that character's game assignment.

## 2. Camp: shared progression and resource competition

### Five villagers and EXP

| Villager | Availability and function |
|---|---|
| **Polonai — Explorer** | Available initially. Levels open caverns, bounded by the released cap. |
| **Kaipu — Engineer** | Rescue in Motherlode, cavern 2. Levels expose schematics; construction separately requires resources. |
| **Cosmo — Conjuror** | Rescue in Bell, cavern 5. Each level supplies one shared Majik point. |
| **Minau — Measurer** | Rescue in Lamp, cavern 7. Levels expose Measurements, each upgraded separately. |
| **Bolaia — Librarian/Cavern Scholar** | Rescue in Evertree, cavern 12. Levels improve Study rate. |

Names/rescue locations are Wiki context; publisher independently confirms Bolaia in cavern 12. Exact rescue flags were not audited. No schematic prerequisite for rescuing villagers was established. [W1, P2, G18]

Opals normally supply **100 EXP/hour each**, or **125** with Opal Dividends, before role/account modifiers. Zero invested Opals means zero ordinary rate in this expression. Rates depend on Majik, Measurements, monument rewards, Bell, collectibles, schematics, and outside-account systems; roles do not share one EXP requirement curve. A purchased villager EXP multiplier is distinct from Majik enhancement. [G1, G3]

Accrual adds `rate × elapsedSeconds / 3600` to saved EXP. The inspected camp handler converts levels for the **selected villager** while its panel is open in The Hole. Therefore enough EXP does not mean the saved unlock already happened. Proposed rows show role, rescue/unlock state, invested Opals, saved level, stored EXP, next requirement, current EXP/hour, and next intrinsic unlock. Browse a role and inspect rate contributors without claiming levels. [G3, G5]

### Opals: sources, allocation, ledger, reset

Cavern sources differ: Well purchases; skilling layer claims; Den score milestones; monument reward offers; Bell Ping; Harp D strings; Lamp's misleadingly named **1000000 Opals** wish, which grants one; Tall jars; Grotto Monarchs; Gambit point milestones; Temple Centurions; Fountain purchases; and Cove Opal Find. External grants/purchases also contribute. Do not model every cavern as the same acquisition action. [G1, G2, G6–G17, W2–W5]

The ledger must distinguish **earned total, invested total, and uninvested supply**, with cavern and external sources. The game's `OpalsOwnedToInvest` reads an actor cache; its refresh caller sums cavern Opals and external grants, then subtracts investments. That cache is not an authoritative saved wallet. External routes include Gem Shop purchases, companions, Grimoire, Compass, Emperor, schematics, Arcane, and Sushi bonuses; current release labels and every grant need reconciliation before attribution. [G1, G3]

Allocation creates genuine competition. Opal Enthusiasm rewards tens invested in a villager; Equal Spread rewards blocks of five in the **least-invested unlocked villager**. Neither establishes a universal best allocation. Hold-down investment is an in-game convenience, not a website control. [G1, G3, G18, P2]

Lamp's **Another Try** costs six wishes and resets **one selected category**: invested Opals, invested Conjuror points, Jar enchantment levels, or Summoning doubler assignments. Opal reset leaves earned Opals, villager levels, and stored EXP intact. Majik reset leaves Cosmo's level intact. Enchantment reset retains discovery level one; doubler reset clears assignments. Wishes spent resetting cannot fund other Lamp benefits. Proposed interaction: inspect ledger and exact reset consequences, never redistribute or execute reset. [G10]

### Kaipu: construction is not unlock

Schematics are one-time account constructions. Available display rows follow Kaipu's level, with three more per level and an extra every fifth level, plus the initial extra row. Stable building ID differs from display order through `HolesInfo[40]`; raw catalog order or index must not become an unlock rule. Source availability caps at 105 rows. Bee String exists in data but Wiki lists it as **Never**; presence is not current player availability. [G1, G3, G18, R1, W1]

Construction rejects already-built entries, checks the real resource/cost, subtracts it, sets the built flag, and consumes the next-schematic Lamp discount. Price can be literal or index-dependent; discount multiplier is `max(0.01, 0.85^stacks)`. Catalog base cost is not necessarily materialized current price. Benefits include buckets, expansion, Den amplifiers, Harp strings, challenge unlocks, production synergies, Studies, later-cavern improvements, and an extra Opal. [G1, G3, R1]

Proposed information: identity, availability requirement, built status, intrinsic effect, actual currency, current price, balance/shortfall, and active discount. Search effects; filter locked, built, or affordable entries. Explain shared-resource competition with Measurements and cavern upgrades beside entries.

### Cosmo: one pool, paths, enhancements, Pocket Divinity

All three Majik trees draw from **one pool**: Cosmo levels plus relevant purchases minus every invested point. Later nodes require the preceding node. Cosmo, Enhance! enables extra enhancement levels; those also consume the same pool. `maxEnhance` describes extra allowance, not necessarily total level cap. Effects are not uniformly linear: Beeg Beeg Forge has a power-of-three branch. [G1, G3]

Hole Majik covers monument benefits, Harp slots, extra wishes, Rupies, and Fountain production. Village Majik covers allocation incentives, construction-based EXP, enhancement, Measurements, Studies, and balanced allocation. Idleon Majik covers Pocket Divinity, forge capacity, multi-resource gains, Ballot Box, Weapon Power, and Equinox. Placeholder Confused Bonus nodes are not released useful upgrades. [G18, R1]

Pocket Divinity stores one or two selected unlocked gods; canonical identity differs from array index. It activates their links account-wide, separate from normal character links. Major/minor callers accept effective Doot or the chosen Pocket god through an **OR**, not duplicate major activation. With effective Doot, Pocket contributes **+15% All Stat per invested level**, or 30% at level two. The tooltip substitutes this benefit for god-selection text, while the underlying link-activation OR remains. All four main stats consume the All Stat contribution. Doot's helper requires the relevant character's Divinity level to reach two, so companion ownership alone is insufficient. Pocket is not useless with Doot. [G1, G3, G4]

Proposed details show pool used/remaining, prerequisites, base/enhanced level and cap, current effective benefits, selected gods, and verified overlap with ordinary links/Doot. Browsing trees is not investing points or choosing gods in-game.

### Minau: all 17 Measurement categories

Each unlocked Measurement spends its mapped cavern resource. Its purchased level supplies a base bonus, strengthened by Lengthmeister, then multiplied by an account statistic. Some base rows saturate rather than scale linearly. The measured stat can grow without another purchase. Show **level, raw measured value and units, multiplier, effective bonus, currency, next cost, and shortfall**, not one unexplained percentage. [G1, G3, G18]

| Measured statistic | All corresponding released effects |
|---|---|
| Account level | Villager EXP; Harp notes |
| Tome score | Bravery maximum sword damage; monument AFK rate |
| Death Note points | Bell Ping rate; Gambit points |
| Slab items | Harp notes; villager EXP; Fountain coin value |
| Crops discovered | Daily Lamp wishes |
| Highest recorded damage | Well bucket rate; Rupie value |
| Total account skill levels | Harp string EXP; Jar production |
| Gloomie kills | Multikill per tier |
| Total Study levels | Rupie value |
| Golem kills | Drop rate |

These groupings cover all **17 rows**. Normalization differs by stat; log-based kills/damage are not raw-count multipliers. Missing Tome/runtime cache inputs must not become false zero progress. Filter by effect or resource and inspect source-stat meaning. [G1, G18]

### Bolaia: targeted and adjacent Studies

Study one unlocked cavern. Target, per-cavern level, and stored progress are saved independently. Gaming Superbit 43 also studies immediate unlocked neighbors at the same rate; it does not spread progress across every cavern. Changing target preserves progress. Rate is progress/hour, with Bolaia, Majik, schematics, collectibles, a stamp, and Fountain inputs. Camp drawing converts sufficient visible-row progress into levels. [G1–G3, G5]

Studies change each cavern's rules: Well expansion; cross-skilling requirements for Motherlode/Hive/Evertree/Trench; Den Golden Hounds; Bravery minimum damage/skips; Bell periodic extra levels; Harp EXP; Lamp wishes; Grotto credited kills; Justice reward window/Opal chance; Jar preferred enchantment; Wisdom attempts/instamatch recovery; Gambit points/attempt preservation; Temple doubled torches; Fountain repeated marbleization; Cove daily discounts. Show target/neighbors, level/progress, next requirement, rate, and actual discrete/scaling effects beside cavern entries. [G2, G18]

### Two separate daily constraints

**Blinding Lantern / Quest90**, sold as 2 Hour Lantern, grants two hours of Hole accrual and villager EXP, excluding skilling-layer progress. Its account-wide daily limit is **12**, checked through `Holes[11][84]`. Consumption directly adds **two lifetime respect hours** to each unlocked released monument and separately adds **7,200 seconds** to pending Hole accrual. Normal elapsed processing advances monument story banks through that accumulator; lifetime respect and story charge remain distinct. Lanterns do not refill every daily action or complete active challenges. Inventory quantity/location remains separate from shared usage. [G5, G10, P3, R1]

**Layer claims** share `OptionsListAccount[318]` across four skilling caverns. Current 1.22 claim source blocks at **six**, whereas Wiki says **five**. Daily rollover resets the counter. Retain this discrepancy until live confirmation; do not silently choose five, give each cavern six, or confuse it with Lantern uses. Exact reset clock remains unknown. [G6, G10, W2–W5]

## 3. All released caverns and proposed website information

Everything described as a player action below happens **in the game**. Website interactions are browsing, detail inspection, searching, filtering, and read-only comparisons. These information needs support the confirmed visibility direction; exact backend contracts and frontend presentation remain for separately authorized work.

### Shared skilling framework

Motherlode, Hive, Evertree, and Trench gather dedicated progress, then manually claim a completed layer for an Opal. Claim resets progress, raises completed count and next requirements, and spends the shared daily allowance. Required resource quantity and required character efficiency are different. The game's displayed efficiency is **0.25 times** `MotherlodeEffBase`, despite that helper serving all four skills. Relevant Studies and Amethyst Heartstone reduce resource requirements across caves. [G1, G6, G18]

For each, proposed information includes layer/depth, gathered/required/remaining resources, displayed efficiency threshold, character-specific relevant efficiency, ready-to-claim status, Opals, and shared allowance. Character comparison is useful; rate/ETA needs real character yield and AFK assumptions. A full progress bar is not an automatic claim. [G6]

### Shared monument framework

Bravery, Justice, and Wisdom have four separate saved concepts: **lifetime credited respect hours**, **manually claimed milestone count**, **stored story-charge seconds**, and **permanent reward levels**. AFK respect grants whole credited hours with bonuses, not fractional elapsed hours. Milestones are sequential claims at 1, 80, 300, 750, 2,000, 5,000, 10,000, and 24,000 hours. Crossing a threshold does not claim it. [G7, G8, G18]

Normal story start requires reward multiplier at least one, snapshots it, and clears the entire story bank—not lifetime hours or rewards. Base growth is one multiplier per 20 banked hours, linear for 48 hours, then diminishing growth rather than a hard cap; modifiers alter both growth and window. Permanent rewards include linear and saturating categories with monument self-bonus, Cosmo, and Fountain effects. Display actual effective benefit and effective cap rather than unboosted text. [G1, G7]

Proposed common details: lifetime hours, claimed/claimable milestone, banked seconds, current story multiplier/window, permanent level/effect table, earned Opals, and saved starting capabilities. Active boards, sword rolls, court currency, and pending rewards are not reconstructible from ordinary save totals. [G7, G12, G14]

### Shallow Caverns: 1–5

**1. Well.** Assign owned buckets to sediments. Negative balance means remaining rock obstruction, not spendable negative stock. Clearing it permits collection; changing upward targets is gated by obstruction. Buckets have individual hourly rates and share target stock. Stock caps depend on sediment and expansions. Schematic-gated auto-expansion spends stock when capped and raises capacity; higher expansion needs its further unlock. Gravel buys escalating-cost Opals. Spending sediment competes with expansion and camp upgrades. Show assignments, obstruction/stock/cap, expansion count/toggle/blockers, bucket and grouped rates, next Opal cost, and gold-bucket effects. Filter obstructed, capped, or spendable bars; inspect rate sources. Offline repeat-expansion behavior is not fully established. [G1, G2, G5, G6, W2]

**2. Motherlode.** Mine dedicated ore, then break a layer under the shared framework. Rescue Kaipu here. Keep current ore, broken layers, and **lifetime ore** separate: lifetime ore survives claims and powers a Well schematic, while layer count powers another synergy. Browse layer and character Mining details. [G6, W1, W2]

**3. Dawg Den.** Charge/reset unlocked amplifiers, then fight until Fear ends the run. Eight amplifiers trade score multiplier against damage, accuracy, healing, size/HP, MP costs, curse/Fear, starting Fear, or earlier Fear. Schematics open amplifiers and stacking benefits. Saved account best **score** earns Opal thresholds; four class-group records are best **kill counts**, which improve buckets, not class scores. Show charges/caps/debuffs, combined multiplier, best score/next threshold, Opals, and Beginner/Warrior/Archer/Mage kill records. Inspect each amplifier and class record. Do not fabricate a live Fear meter or predicted survival. [G1, G5, G6, W2]

**4. Bravery.** Throw swords, choose a chest after a win, then continue or flee. Rewards remain pending until fleeing; defeat loses them. Rethrow only the last resolved sword, replacing its damage and spending a charge. A retelling restores the current battle/checkpoint, not an escape choice. Saved respect/milestones improve starting swords, rethrows, retelling, and damage; remaining rethrows and battle streak also affect active damage. Benefits cover Mining, buckets, Cooking, villagers, Gaming, damage, Bell, monument AFK, own reward scaling, and Opal odds. Show shared monument details, best Last Stand, saved starting capabilities, and baseline damage sources. Inspect milestones/rewards and read loss-versus-bank rules; active rolls and pending chests stay absent. [G1, G7, W2]

**5. Bell.** Select **Ring, Ping, Clean, or Renew**; only selected mode accumulates charge, while separate banks persist. Ring raises random permanent bonuses; Ping gives an Opal; Clean attempts another improvement method; Renew clears Ring bank/count and bonus levels while retaining Ping, methods, improvement levels, and Opals. Renew is not Clean. Six improvement methods spend coins, Mythril, Gaming bits, Eighth Notes, atoms, or green Rupies. Seven current bonus families include Fountain coin gain, despite Wiki's six-row shallow table. Clean failure pity is **linear** in source, not repeated 1.25× compounding implied by text. Show all mode banks/rates/costs, methods/next resource costs, failures/current odds, bonus levels/effects, and explicit Renew consequences. Browse modes and filter improvements by currency or affordability. [G1, G5, G6, W2, P3]

### Glowshroom Tunnels: 6–10

**6. Harp.** Save tune and string layout; buy notes and drag across strings to strum. At least 100% power begins a rewarded strum, consuming **all stored power** as one snapshot. Each slot rewards once; regeneration pauses during strum. Unassigned owned types still provide passive level bonuses. C yields the selected note; D rolls an Opal; E aids power; F awards nearby notes; G grants other types EXP; A awards every known note. B has no established useful effect and Wiki lists its schematic unavailable. Strings gain EXP/levels; ten notes unlock using the highest current note. Domino makes order matter, Variety makes layout diversity matter, and a successful D pluck changes later Opal odds. Show power/hour, saved power/layout/tune, owned types/passives, slots, string EXP, note balances and next cost. Inspect types/notes without presenting one fixed strum outcome or silently inferring transient order. [G1, G9, G18, W1, W3]

**7. Lamp.** Bank daily wishes, unlock wish types, and spend on selected effects. Daily restock is `floor(averageDailyWishes + randomFloat())`: fractional rate is an expectation, not guaranteed extra wishes. Besides resets, wishes buy one Opal, add 12 permanent respect hours to a chosen monument, stack next-schematic discount, boost resources, or supply World 4/5/6/7 benefits. Source applies additional account scaling; base text is not final effect. Knowledge of Future and World 8 descriptions remain unsupported future effects. Show wish stock, expected daily gain, unlock/purchase progression, prices, permanent benefits, discount stacks, and reset categories. Search wishes and inspect costs/consequences; no purchase/reset control. [G1, G10, W3]

**8. Undying Hive.** Catch Fractalfly toward a harvestable layer. Catching efficiency is relevant, not Mining despite the shared helper. Completed layers strengthen Harp via its schematic; current flies do not substitute for layers. Show shared skilling information and owned Harp synergy; inspect Catching capability and requirement details. [G6, G9, W3]

**9. Gloomie Mushroom Grotto.** Kill ordinary mushrooms toward colony quota, then trigger and defeat a separate Monarch for an Opal. Monarch HP grows with cleared colonies. Current colony kills reset; lifetime **credited kills** persist and can include multikill/Study weighting. Schematics turn cleared colonies into drop rate, class EXP, villager EXP, and respawn benefits. Show colony, kill progress/quota, readiness, Monarch HP, lifetime record, Opals, and owned synergy. Browse combat requirements and benefit sources. Statue/class-respawn tips remain secondary guidance, not audited recommendations. [G1, G2, G11, W3, P2, P3]

**10. Justice.** Approve, reject, or dismiss court cases using temporary coins, mental health, popularity, and dismissals. Cases include immediate costs, affordability gates, loans, investments, promises, forced choices, ongoing popularity/coin changes, special dismissal outcomes, and random effects. Story “days” often advance by case transitions, not daily reset. Timmy's sequence can award a permanent achievement. Earned retirement chests yield chosen rewards after court ends; settlement then commits permanent levels/Opals. Benefits cover Catching, Harp, artifacts, villagers, Summoning, class EXP, wishes, monument AFK, self-scaling, and Opal odds. Show common monument progress and saved starting capabilities. Browse/search cases by NPC, currency, or consequence, explaining continuing effects beside immediate deltas. Current case, flags, court wallet, and unsettled rewards remain actor-only; a case browser is not a greedy strategy engine. [G1, G12, G18, W3]

### Underground Overgrowth: 11–15

**11. Jars.** Select production types, let jars form on a saved board, then break them. Ten types produce basic/decent/elegant Rupies, Opal chance, new collectibles, enchantments, white Rupies, a gilded bonus, dark Rupies, or master Rupies. There are **12 currencies**: standard/master balances plus separate white/dark counters. Current holdings gate colors and next jar purchases. Up to three producers and break-all are schematic-gated. Quality scales rewards; gilded jars store a bonus consumed by the next Rupie-paying jar, so order matters. All **40 collectibles** have saved levels: discovery sets one, each enchant adds one repeatedly. First enchant doubles level one; it is not a binary enchant flag. Study's preferred target biases rather than guarantees enchantment. Effects cover currency, production, chances, villagers, skilling requirements, Well/Bell/Harp/Studies/monuments/Gambit, plus explicitly future descriptions. Show board/type/quality, production work/rate, all wallets/gates, next jar cost, pending gilded bonus, collectible levels/effects, and preferred target. Filter missing, enchanted, or benefit categories. Exact offline conversion remains unaudited. [G1, G2, G13, G18, W4]

**12. Evertree.** Chop Everlogs and whittle trunks for Opals under the shared framework. Rescue Bolaia here. Trunk Studies reduce other skilling requirements. Show Choppin efficiency, wood/trunk progress, shared claims, rescue context, and cross-cavern effect; browse character capability. [G6, G18, W1, W4, P2]

**13. Wisdom.** Spend normal story charge on matching cards, use instamatches, clear boards, and choose rewards. Saved milestones/respect/Studies determine starting attempts, gains per clear, and instamatches. Pure-memory mode has distinct rules: 30 attempts, no per-clear gains or instamatches, and a different timer; its entry preserves the normal bank in inspected source. Normal board/attempts/reveals and pending rewards are transient. Benefits cover Choppin, Rupies, Jade, villagers, Farming, drop rate, Gambit, monument AFK, self-scaling, and Opal odds. Show common monument data and saved starting capabilities; inspect normal/pure rules and reward/milestone details. No hidden-card answers or assumed active board. Default to normal-mode information; keep secret-mode descriptions discoverable without selecting that mode by default. [G1, G2, G7, G14, W4, P2]

**14. Gambit.** Six Summoning-style challenges are King survival, Horsey one HP, Bishop reflected damage, Queen all-jeweled cards, Castle one lane, and Noob gray slimes. Schematics unlock later challenges. Saved best survival seconds drive points; current multipliers can raise total points without new records. Normally a shared daily flag limits entry; Study can probabilistically preserve the attempt, not guarantee two attempts. Summoning doubler assignments are separate saved rewards reset through Lamp. Nineteen reward slots include sixteen named current descriptions and three future/unknown effects: doublers, Opals, Flurbos, resources, stones, essence, ribbons, coins, Owl/Roo, Construction, Snail Mail, stealth, bones, bubbles, Spelunking, and Research. Do not claim all nineteen released useful effects. Source score parenthesization differs from Wiki shorthand; ribbon extra-rank applicability has exclusions, including rank 20+ in publisher context. Show challenge rules/unlocks/records/points, base/effective total, contributors, next reward, daily flag, and doublers/assignments. Browse rewards and challenge details, not predicted survival. [G2, G15, G18, W4, P2, P3]

**15. Temple.** Kill Ancient Golems for torches. Bonfire spends them through three actions: **Illuminate** improves search, **Search** can awaken a Centurion, **Amplify** improves active-only respawn. Successful awakening resets Illuminate immediately; death increments Sanctum and grants an Opal. Torch doubling has shared bonus inputs. There is no separately established bonfire level/currency. Show Sanctum, torches, action prices/effects/affordability, current displayed Search chance, reset consequence, active-only label, torch sources, Opals, and intrinsic drop context. Inspect actions or drop details. Search purchase ordering and randomness prevent guaranteed Opal timelines. [G2, G16, W4]

### Sentinel Passages: 16–18

**16. Fountain.** Fill bars, generate random eligible currencies onto stacks, collect them, buy upgrades, and marbleize eligible upgrades. Distinguish nine-currency **spendable wallet**, saved **uncollected stack arrays/royal flags**, and actor stack images. Overflow partially credits wallet. Ignored currencies change eligibility; desired currency changes value. Effective capacity is capped at **16 positions × 50 height**, even if purchased levels grow. Later currency families use different value scaling. [G2, G17, G18, W5]

Three released upgrade pages contain **60 slots**: Regular covers currencies, capacity/overflow, fill/active speed, Bravery/Cosmo, golden buckets and global benefits; Yellow adds bills, royal stacks, marble, desire/ignore, Justice/Studies/Harp and global benefits; Green adds stack currencies, luck/ducks, Wisdom, Measurement costs, Jar enchantments and global benefits. Displayed water navigates upgrades, not exclusive production. Red Water's present multiplier description does not establish a released red page; Oldmoney is not a generated tenth currency. [G2, G17, G18, W5, P3]

Marble **amount**, base upgrade **level**, and per-upgrade marbleization **level** differ. Study enables repeated marbleization; excluded upgrades remain ineligible. Collection rolls permanent per-currency luck; duck-bar completion rolls a duck rather than guaranteeing one. Lucky counts/ducks improve value, so pending stack valuation can change during collection. Source also contains increasing-cost direct Opal purchases; later currency reachability needs reconciliation. [G2, G17]

Proposed information includes every wallet, pending stack/royal state and snapshot value, ignore/desire setting, rate/bar progress, effective capacity/occupancy/overflow, all upgrade prerequisites/currency/cost/effects, marble amount/eligibility/levels, luck/ducks, and Opals. Browse pages, filter locked/affordable/marble-eligible upgrades, inspect value sources. Do not equate upgraded capacity with effective capacity or promise a specific next currency/duck.

**17. Bottomless Trench.** Fish dedicated Trench Fish, then Cast completed depths for Opals. Higher depths raise requirements; Studies feed cross-skilling reductions, while a schematic ties depth to Fountain value. Show Fishing capability and the shared layer information; inspect synergy and remaining daily claims. Wiki's missing efficiency table does not mean source lacks a threshold. [G1, G2, G6, G18, W5]

**18. Crystal Glunko Cove.** Kill Crystal Glunkos and pick up **12 special shapes**, recorded in account balances rather than ordinary inventory. Blue and purple boosted selections are saved separately. **24 upgrade slots** include local DR, AFK, multikill, respawn and pickup effects, currency-sensitive collectors, costs, global bonuses, an Opal, and rank-15 Cooking ribbon; IDK Broh remains explicitly future/unknown. Source overrides normal DR here, and normal stats may still be inputs. Show Cove-local outputs with local labels, not ordinary account DR/AFK values. Study discounts a number of first daily purchases by 15%; the counter is not a daily purchase cap. Show shapes/boosted targets, kills, upgrade levels/currencies/prices/effects/shortfalls, local/global scope, discount allowance, and earned rewards. Filter blue/purple, local/global, affordable, or owned entries and inspect each stat source. Digit/log-based collectors need exact source semantics at powers of ten. [G2, G16, G18, W5, P3]

## 4. Confirmed first-pass outcomes and boundaries

**Confirmed baseline:** A player can understand the entire feature's current progression and requirements, distinguish owned from possible benefits, inspect verified capability, stats and next costs, see resource competition, and recognize shared limits. Descriptions belong beside relevant entries, not in a mandatory enormous wiki. Current deterministic arithmetic is useful even when it consumes cross-account modifiers; inaccurate inputs must remain unknown, not fake zero.

1. **Visibility and verified capability.** Current progression, effective benefits, costs, shortfalls, and verified capability comparisons are the focus. Existing source-backed rate information may describe recorded state, but an efficiency/rate engine, simulation, hypothetical allocation planner, strategy helper, and recommendations are outside this first pass.
2. **Released and locked content.** Show everything in the released feature, including locked entries, by default. Where reasonable, provide a **Show unlocked** checkbox that restricts the view. No secret-mode view is selected by default; secret-mode descriptions remain discoverable with other released information. Source-only future placeholders are still not released content.
3. **Snapshot-based information.** Do not advance saved production, balances, readiness, or progress using elapsed time between snapshot/cloud-save and current time. Show recorded state and verified current-state calculations without implying live freshness. Forecasts are not a first-pass focus; no countdown or timer is authorized by this scope confirmation.

Read-only visibility never authorizes spending, constructing, allocating, equipping, assigning characters, claiming, starting challenges, opening jars, ringing/cleaning/renewing, or advancing the game.

## 5. Factual gaps and current coverage

These gaps do not reduce scope to existing parser coverage or prevent formalizing outcomes. Separately authorized backend work must verify data ownership, source inputs, and affected calculations; frontend work must verify labels, presentation, and actual player-facing behavior. Unverified outputs must not be presented as established facts.

- **Live parity and rescue:** No connected live account or Hole screen; exact rescue flags, entry enforcement, and source-only availability need confirmation.
- **Daily/reset semantics:** Reconcile source-six/Wiki-five layer claims before presenting an authoritative remaining-claims total. Twelve Lantern uses are a separate confirmed source/publisher limit. Reset clock/timezone and imported timestamp meaning are not first-pass countdown requirements.
- **Rates and offline behavior:** Verify character capability inputs and any displayed rates, Well expansion behavior, Jar board semantics, active Fountain modifiers, and Lantern effects where relevant to current-state information. Detailed elapsed-time bridges and forecast behavior are not first-pass requirements.
- **State/save mapping:** Complete persistent-state mapping and export behavior across accounts; do not invent current minigame boards, pending rewards, actor selections, or contribution history.
- **Static completeness:** Existing catalogs cover many families, including buildings, Majik, Measurements, Studies, Bell, jars/collectibles, Gambit, Fountain, and shapes. No specific missing static field was demonstrated by the bounded catalog search. Full value/description/current-version parity remains unaudited; no catalog-lag conclusion follows from nominal counts. [R1]
- **Effective/downstream semantics:** Resolve all modifier/cap inputs, other god-link alternatives, price currencies, stochastic branches, and external additive/multiplicative callers before claiming calculator parity. Pocket's Doot All Stat alternative is verified in source, but full personalized aggregation is not. Clean pity, Bell's seventh bonus, Fountain effective caps, and Gambit score wording show why text alone is insufficient. [G1, G2, G4, G6, G15, G17]

Existing backend collections and source-calculation history are a footprint, not exhaustive parser or product authority. Closed issues **#384, #364, and #357** record prior selected correctness work. The earlier bounded docs/tracker search found no broad Hole product approval; the human's first-pass direction is now recorded in this brief, not a published delivery specification. The hidden UI remains excluded entirely. [R2]

The connected `http://127.0.0.1:3100/status` request timed out after 5,001 ms. Offline status reported `source: offline`, `cdpConnected: true`, `injected: true`, `gameReady: true`, and paused virtual time. An unsupported `/game-version` route returned 404; that was not runtime failure. [O1]

Harp power `48885.69767204844`, wish stock `3128`, colony clears `12`, current/lifetime kills `1901637656.7288694 / 7841653999.9918375`, and Justice hours/claimed milestones `[24090,8]` demonstrate distinct state meanings. ### Offline assigned-character Mining observation — blocked

The saved assignment snapshot places Motherlode assignments at character slots 6 and 9; active live slot 3 is unassigned. Live `SkillStats` calls accept no character-index argument, so matching assigned-character efficiency outputs remain unavailable from that runtime. The existing paired live `/cloud-save` and Hole-state observations remain in the preceding runtime evidence; no new live request was made for this investigation.

The offline tool accepts `--character INDEX` and `--port PORT`. Its README says `--character` selects a zero-based `playerNames` slot through original UI handlers and `/cloud-save` returns startup input only. Separate instances could load the same save path and separate loopback ports, but that does not make startup read-only with respect to gameplay.

Startup source proves the safety blocker: `runtime.cjs` enters the original importer, invokes the original logout handler twice, installs captured save data, selects the requested character through an original UI click, clicks original Play, and initializes the selected scene (`runtime.cjs:196-221`). It then performs an original same-scene refresh (`runtime.cjs:233-241`). This crosses the explicit no-gameplay boundary. Although the tool isolates its browser from the live game and does not persist to the real server or source save, startup performs game lifecycle actions in the offline instance. Therefore no instance was started.

No assigned-character Mining efficiency outputs or paired offline runtime Hole values were collected. Exact expressions cannot be reported as successful observations. Required next evidence remains blocked unless a startup path can select/load the requested saved character without invoking gameplay or state-changing original handlers, or the no-gameplay constraint changes. Existing live assignment and Hole observations do not establish slot 6/9 skill outputs.

Evidence: [offline tool README](../../sub-projects/idleon-offline/README.md):16-33,54-65,94-95; [startup lifecycle](../../sub-projects/idleon-offline/runtime.cjs):196-221,233-241; [HTTP server](../../sub-projects/idleon-offline/server.cjs):45-49,68-93. No version request, instance startup, gameplay, claim, reset, or save mutation occurred during this follow-up.

**Research-phase boundary:** The human approved this brief and authorized tracker publication on 2026-10-12, with an explicit stop afterward. Evidence collection performed source/state reads, not game actions. No delivery plan, backend/frontend plan, or implementation starts automatically.
### Part 4 v1.23 real-save parity route investigation — 2026-10-17

**Result:** No applicable paired v1.23 real-save/output route was found in the inspected repository or running offline server. The installed runtime is v1.23, but its loaded save is the single `latest.json` fixture, not a different identified v1.23 save. Existing Hole extraction outputs are from that same fixture path unless their records prove otherwise; results do not establish independent save provenance.

**Canonical access and server check:** Followed [game-access policy](../../tests/helpers/README.md#game-access), which defaults to offline and requires same-server readiness/version checks. Read-only requests to `http://127.0.0.1:3101/status` returned HTTP 200 with `source:"offline"`, `cdpConnected:true`, `injected:true`, `gameReady:true`, `stage:"ready"`, selected index `3`, name `Sludgev4`. `GET /game-version` returned `{"title":"Luminous_Menagerie","version":"1.23"}`. These establish the running assets and readiness, not save version/provenance.

**Save and fixture routes checked:**

- Read-only `GET /cloud-save` succeeded. It contains one account with 11 player names (`Sludgadin`, `Sludgev2`, `Sludgev3`, `Sludgev4`, `Sludgev5`, `Sludgev6`, `SludgeMan`, `Sludgev8`, `Sludgev9`, `Sludgev10`, `Sludgev11`) and one account-level `Holes` field.
