### Part 4 phase-5 v1.23 Well and Bell saved-state mapping — 2026-10-17

**Well bucket assignment (`Holes[10]`):** Source uses each saved bucket value as an index into sediment stock `Holes[9]` (`idleon1.23.txt:261633–641`, `265588–592`). The menu blocks increment at value `9` and decrement at value `0`; it therefore treats `9` as the upper/unassigned sentinel and permits saved values `0–9` (`263566–576`). A displayed stock of `|` means the indexed sediment stock is negative, not that assignment is unassigned (`261633–640`). Source does not define a distinct “unassigned” value outside the sediment-index range: value `9` is both used as the assignment sentinel and indexes `Holes[9][9]` in display/production expressions. Thus the sentinel interpretation is supported by menu guards, while its overlap with the tenth stock index is a source ambiguity; do not claim all ten sediment indices can be assigned or that `9` never participates in production.

**Bell levels (`Holes[17][0..11]`):** The game calculates each level's effect as `Holes[17][t] × HolesInfo[59][2*t+1]` (`240969`). The Bell UI loops over all twelve saved indices and reads labels from `HolesInfo[59][2*n]` (`262070–103`). The generated `BellBonusRepo` contains seven indexed records only: index 0 Bucket Fill Rate, 1 All Villager EXP, 2 Harp Note Gains, 3 Daily Lamp Wishes, 4 Extra Rupie Chance, 5 Double Torch Chance, 6 Coins from Fountain (`data/domain/data/BellBonusRepo.ts:7–16`). No source mapping from twelve saved level slots to those seven repository records is defined. Code directly pairs slot `n` with flattened metadata pair `n`, so only slots 0–6 align with the seven static records; slots 7–11 are not mapped by any evidenced rule. Do not infer family/label/effect assignments for those five slots.

**Evidence limits:** These are static v1.23 source facts, not live-game observations. No runtime or website evidence was used.

#### Jar type identity, production-rate, and image research — 2026-10-19

**Access and type identity:** v1.23 catalogs ten identities at indices 0–9. Generated `HoleJarRepo.ts:9–24` names them Simple, Tall, Ornate, Great, Enchanted, Artisan, Epic, Gilded, Ceremony, and Heirloom Jar. Heirloom is ID 9 (`data/domain/data/HoleJarRepo.ts:23–24`). `Holes[11][37]` is the number of paid type unlocks, not a count including initial Simple Jar: `JarTypesOwned` returns that saved number; next purchase is allowed while it is `< 9`, and each purchase increments it (`idleon1.23.txt:241160,241168–173`; purchase caller `265397–435`). The selector arrows prove the mapping: at count N, current type N is the rightmost allowed assignment, and type 0 is the leftmost; at count 0, assignment 0 is valid (`262541–549`). Therefore the accessible type range is inclusive `0..ownedTypeCount`, and correct access is `typeIndex <= ownedTypeCount`. The source caps paid count at 9, making all ten types available, including Heirloom 9. Current parser code incorrectly uses `ownedTypeCount >= jar.index + 1` (`data/domain/world-5/hole/jar.tsx:126–131`); this marks Simple locked at count 0 and Heirloom locked at count 9. Correct comparison is `ownedTypeCount >= jar.index`. Count 10 is not reachable through the purchase predicate. Source selector behavior establishes access boundaries; no live assignment action was attempted.

**Rate contract:** `JarProductionPerHR` returns work units per hour, not jars per hour: source formula is `36,000 × (1 + (collectible bonuses 1,15,24 + Measurement 12)/100) × (1 + B_UPG(72,10) × log10(Holes[11][38])/100)` (`idleon1.23.txt:241227–233`; log helper `103818–820`). Each producer accumulates that work by elapsed seconds divided by 3,600. Its selected Jar type sets threshold `JarProductionREQ(type) = (1000 + 2000×type) / ((1+B_UPG(67,30)/100) × (1 + B_UPG(74,5)×log10(Holes[11][max(0,type−1)+40])/100))` (`241161–166,265623–647`). On reaching threshold, one Jar is created and saved work is not reset; the source also stores quality as `floor(log10(work/requirement))`, which affects Jar quality rather than quantity (`265635–647`). Therefore expected completed Jars/hour per assigned producer is `JarProductionPerHR / JarProductionREQ(type)`, while its persisted work/hour remains the raw work rate. No type-independent raw rate may be displayed as Jars/hour.

The retained matched v1.23 extraction provides a concrete example: producer 0 has 788,162.8901608335 work/hour, type 4 requirement 5,395.485805444112, and inferred production 146.08 Jars/hour (source formula quotient, not separately runtime-extracted completed-count rate). Requirements for type 4 do not stand in for other types. This supersedes the earlier unresolved image-identifier and CDN-availability statements at lines 4695 and 4718. The v1.23 game source and current CDN resolve all requested images.

**Exact index rules**

- Jar type ID `i` (0–9) → `HoleJar{i}.png`, native CDN PNG dimensions 67×71. The v1.23 board renderer builds `"HoleJar" + savedJarType + ".png"` (`idleon1.23.txt:269017–033`). The generated catalog names the IDs Simple, Tall, Ornate, Great, Enchanted, Artisan, Epic, Gilded, Ceremony, and Heirloom (`data/domain/data/HoleJarRepo.ts:9–24`).
- Collectible index `i` (0–39) → `HoleJarC{i}.png`, dimensions 41×41. The v1.23 collectible UI initializes all 40 images with `"HoleJarC" + n + ".png"` (`idleon1.23.txt:269236`), direct index identity without exceptions.
- Rupie wallet currency ID `20+i` (i=0–9) → `HoleJarR{i}.png`, dimensions 25×25. Generated `HoleCurrencyRepo.ts:101–110` confirms IDs 20–29 have kind `Rupie`, localIndex 0–9, and names Rupie 0–9.
- Special Jar holdings `Holes[11][38]` and `[39]` represent Rupie reward types 10 and 11, respectively; use `HoleJarR10.png` and `HoleJarR11.png`, each 25×25. `JarRupieTypeGiven` maps Jar type 5 to 10 and type 8 to 11 (`idleon1.23.txt:241257–280`); the reward caller writes type 10 into `[11][38]` and type 11 into `[11][39]` (`268909–913`). These are special Rupie holdings, not Fountain currencies. In particular, `[11][39]` is not Fountain’s missing resource/currency ID 39.

**Image evidence:** `assets/distBuild/static/game/N.js` registers all three contiguous filename series: `HoleJar0`–`HoleJar9`, `HoleJarC0`–`HoleJarC39`, and `HoleJarR0`–`HoleJarR11`. The game uses type IDs directly for Jar assets and collectible indices directly for collectible assets; the Rupie type and wallet mappings are supported by source and generated currency identities above. Read-only GET requests to `https://cdn2.idleonefficiency.com/images/{filename}` returned HTTP 200 and `image/png` for every one of the 62 files; none were missing. PNG IHDR dimensions matched 67×71, 41×41, and 25×25 by family. No CDN asset publication occurred.

**Existing metadata/API reuse:** `components/base/IconImage.tsx:7–20` resolves `ImageData.location` through the canonical CDN base and appends `.png`; `data/domain/imageData.ts` defines the metadata shape. `HoleCurrency` already exposes nullable `imageData` and `getImageData()` (`data/domain/world-5/hole/hole.tsx:70–120`), but its handwritten `holeCurrencyImages` map currently omits IDs 20–24 and 26–29. Existing entries 25 and 31–38 are unrelated partial mappings. Extend/reuse this owner for wallet currencies rather than adding a second currency map.

Jar catalogs have no generated art field. `HoleJarModel` is name/description only; `HoleJarBonusModel` is name/bonus/`filler1`/description. All 40 bonus records’ `filler1` values are literal `"Filler"` (for example `HoleJarBonusRepo.ts:9–19`); they do not encode an image ID. `HoleCurrencyModel.icon` is a game glyph marker, not `ImageData` (`data/domain/model/holeCurrencyModel.ts:3–9`). No generated filler or icon field supplies these mappings. Use explicit `ImageData` at the existing Jar presentation/domain boundary; no generated-data prerequisite, extraction, or CDN upload is needed.

**Observed lifecycle evidence:** `IdleonData.initAccountDataKeys` calls each domain's `init` and stores returned instances (`data/domain/idleonData.tsx:255–272`). `updateIdleonData` parses each domain after inserting its initialized instance and runs ordered post-processing (`:453–505`); Hole calculation is split between `updateHole` and late `updateHolePresentation` (`data/domain/world-5/hole/hole.tsx:2451–2632`, registered at `idleonData.tsx:278–447`). `Hole.init` returns `this` (`hole.tsx:2237–2256`); aspect instances and static catalogues are constructed as Hole fields (`:1817–1848`). #### Hole DATA-01 nullable-contract audit — completed inventory — 2026-10-20

This closes the earlier partial audit. It is a repository contract audit, not a game-semantic verification. All cited line numbers refer to the current handwritten implementation. No production code, tests, or temporary artifacts were changed or run.

**Lifecycle proof and boundary limit**

- `initAccountDataKeys` stores each initialized domain (`data/domain/idleonData.tsx:255–272`); `updateIdleonData` gives that instance to its parser, then runs ordered post-processing (`:453–505`). `Hole.init` returns itself, and creates catalogues/aspects (`data/domain/world-5/hole/hole.tsx:1813–1848,2237–2256`). Therefore initialized Hole, Jar, Fountain, Cove, Well, Bell, Harp, Lamp, and their static catalogue rows are required objects, not nullable values.
- `HandleRawDataKey` supplies each declared raw default (`data/domain/base/domain.tsx:48–63`). Hole declares `Holes` default `[]`, `Jars` default `null` (`hole.tsx:2225–2234`). Parsing fills missing Hole rows as `[]`; it deliberately restores `undefined` for selected aspect inputs (`:2258–2268`). An omitted raw field and an absent initialized domain object are different contracts.
- `rawData` is the original cloud-save object (`idleonData.tsx:457,492`), not the map of keys after defaults. Thus a `sourceSaveAvailable` test against raw keys can record real input absence, even when another parser receives its declared default. This proves the flag detects absence; it does not prove every absent field is a supported/current-save state, nor justify nullable domain objects.
- Do not remove `sourceSaveAvailable` by assuming either “all keys exist” or “empty save is supported.” Keep only flags whose calculation genuinely requires an optional persisted input and for which absence has defined unavailable semantics. Confirm support from the importer/game save contract before removing a raw-field gate. This audit found no evidence that Missing save properties mean numeric zero for the flagged cross-domain systems.

**Finishable correction groups**

Replace only fixed-ID/index lookups guarded as if the object could be absent. Candidates: optional `bell.bonuses[6]` passed to Fountain (`:2544`); optional `bell.bonuses[0]` in Well (`well.tsx:122`); optional `bell.bonuses[3]` in Lamp (`hole.tsx:1726`); optional Cosmo lookup in Lamp (`:1724,1728`); optional schematic lookup in `Well.prepare` (`well.tsx:116–119`) and fixed `schematics.find(...)?` use in Gambit (`hole.tsx:2524`); Hole init's optional `measurements.find(...)?` at `:2249–2252` is the deliberate exception for optional currency image metadata. #### Hole priority-2 Villager lifecycle correction — 2026-10-20

**Cause:** `Villager.nextUnlock` is required state, but `Villager.parse` only loads saved levels and related raw state. The existing `Villager.prepareNextUnlock` correctly assigns all five variants through `Hole.prepareInspection`; however, `Hole.prepareInspection` had no caller. The normal import therefore reached UI consumers with unprepared `nextUnlock`, and `nextUnlock(villager, hole)` threw while reading `atMaximum` or `kind`. This was a missing producer call, not an invalid optional state or a branch requiring a fallback.

**Correction:** `updateHolePresentation` now calls `hole.prepareInspection()` unconditionally after its presentation inputs and upgrade inspection are prepared. This late stage runs after the regular calculation pipeline and before UI consumption. It preserves `Hole.prepareInspection`'s existing reset-preview preparation and keeps all five unlock values owned by `Villager.prepareNextUnlock`. No UI guards, fallback values, save fields, readiness flags, or release-version logic were added.

**Regression coverage:** The normal-import test now compares complete `nextUnlock` objects for all five Villagers, including `kind`, `requiredLevel`, `identities`, and `atMaximum`. A producer test covers level-zero/unrescued state for all five, and maximum states for Polonai, Kaipu, and Minau. Cosmo and Bolaia remain complete with `atMaximum: false` and empty identities. The test restores every mutated level in `finally` and recalculates the imported previews afterward.

**Before / after:** Before this correction, `part5-state.test.ts` was 32/33 and failed at `nextUnlock.kind`; the actual browser route failed at `nextUnlock.atMaximum`. After the correction, all five complete preview records exist on normal import, the selected max/unrescued branches produce complete records, and the actual route renders all five Villager cards without a task-specific exception.

**Verification:** `yarn test tests/domains/hole/part5-state.test.ts tests/domains/hole/opal-ledger.test.ts tests/domains/hole/studies.test.ts --runInBand` passed: 3 suites, 60 tests. #### Jar board quantity and Rupie-value prerequisites — 2026-10-20

**Board contract:** v1.23 persists board entries in `Jars`; accepted parsing maps entry `[0]` to type and `[1]` to quality and limits the board to 120 entries (`jar.tsx:135–153`; game source `idleon1.23.txt:265631–647`). Existing static owner is `HoleJarRepo` / `JarType`; no separate board-capacity static data is needed. Implement per-type physical count as count of valid board entries by type, and Quantity as sum of `10 ** quality` for those entries. Global count is all parsed entries; global Quantity is sum across every type, including hidden types and zero-count types. Empty types have count 0 and Quantity 0. Mixed qualities, e.g. q0 + q2 + q2, mean count 3 and Quantity 201. These are board summaries, not forecast or reward-payout claims. Preserve existing producer rates and `Show all=false`.

**Rupie formula:** v1.23 `idleon1.23.txt:241234–251` defines `JarRupieValue` as an ordered product:
`(1 + B_UPG(62,1) + B_UPG(65,2) + B_UPG(68,4)) × max(1,1.5^OptionsListAccount[355]) × (1+LampBonuses(99,0)/400) × (1+MonumentROGbonuses(2,1)/100) × (1+(MeasurementBonusTOTAL(10,0)+MeasurementBonusTOTAL(14,0))/100) × max(1,B_UPG(80,1)×1.1^Holes[11][5]) × (1+Holes[11][60]/100) × (1+JarCollectibleBonus(3,0)/100) × (1+JarCollectibleBonus(17,0)/100) × (1+JarCollectibleBonus(28,0)/100) × (1+(JarCollectibleBonus(0,0)+JarCollectibleBonus(6,0)+JarCollectibleBonus(13,0)+JarCollectibleBonus(21,0)+JarCollectibleBonus(33,0))/100) × (1+StampBonusOfTypeX("CavernRes")/100) × (1+Cglunko_upgBon(14,0)/100)`.
The formula returns a numeric base Rupie value, not total reward. Native reward resolution multiplies by `10^quality` (`268905–918`). The inspected source exposes no rounding in formula; display formatting rounds only the sub-1000 `Small` path, uses comma notation below 1e9, and `Big` notation otherwise (`262605–620`). Player-facing unit is Rupies per Rupie; no guaranteed board payout follows from this base value.

**Original API note superseded by matched-runtime continuation below.** The model already exposes the typed owners listed in the continuation. `updateHole` currently runs before `updateStamps`; calculate Jar Rupie Value only after stamp bonuses are prepared.

**Description:** Only `ABNORMAL RUPIE` has `$` in existing `HoleJarBonusRepo` descriptions (`HoleJarBonusRepo.ts:9–13`). Native collectible-description code substitutes `$` only for collectible index 0. It uses `JarRupieValue`: `<1000` via `NotateNumber(...,"Small")`; `<1e9` via `CommaNotation`; otherwise `NotateNumber(...,"Big")` (`idleon1.23.txt:262605–620`). `$` means current Jar Rupie Value, not literal currency symbol. Native description first substitutes collectible `%` separately.

**Runtime mismatch claim corrected:** The cited SHA-256 values represented different data encodings: canonical runtime JSON versus raw fixture-file bytes. Comparing them did not establish a save mismatch. The continuation below deep-compares parsed runtime and fixture JSON and records native parity; no save restoration or user action was warranted.
